hero.name: Rodrigo Alarcão
hero.statement:
I take ideas from concept to MVP in weeks —
not decks, not prototypes. Working products.

body: I'm a product designer who builds.
Seven years designing complex B2B systems taught me how products really work — the messy parts, the edge cases, the decisions that only make sense when you've shipped something real.

Then I started building. Not switching careers — expanding what design means to me. I use AI as a tool, not a shortcut. I developed my own methodology to go from a raw idea to a live product with consistency and quality.

In 2026 I launched two products independently. One of them — a civic participation platform — I built solo in ten days using Claude Code. No technical co-founder. No handoff to a developer. Just process, judgment, and the right tools.
I'm looking for founders and teams who need someone that thinks about product, designs with intent, and ships without waiting for permission.

methodology.intro:
Every product I build follows the same system.
Four steps, documented before the first line of code.

steps.title: Discovery
steps.body: Understanding the idea before touching any tool. What should this feel like? Who is it for? What's the emotional core? I use a VIBE-PRD — a document that captures intent and personality before any technical decision.

steps.title: Strategy
steps.body: Choosing the right stack, defining the design system, documenting every decision. My Foundation and Decision Framework ensure nothing is improvised. When building starts, every question already has an answer.

steps.title: Design & Build
steps.body: Design and code happen together. No Figma handoff, no gap between what's designed and what's built. Using AI-assisted development, I move from wireframe to working product in days — iterating in the browser, not in a static file.

steps.title: Launch
steps.body: A working product in production. Deployed, tested, real. Not a prototype that lives in a presentation — an MVP that users can touch. Then: feedback, iteration, and scale.
